# Paris Trip — Itinerary (June 2026)

Quick brain-dump for the Paris demo trip. Will refine
once the return is sorted.

## Meeting

- Client demo at **Paris Nord Villepinte, Hall 5** on **Tue 9 June 2026,
  15:00 CEST**. Showing them the HexaScan 500 live on their parts, so
  I need to be there with time to unpack and calibrate the kit.

## Travel

- Fly out of **SFO on Mon 8 June**, which puts me in Paris the morning
  of the 9th.
- Return on **12 June**. I'll book that later once the client confirms
  the follow-up day.

## Needs

- Arrive **CDG** on **9 June** with a few hours before the 15:00 meeting
  to unpack and calibrate. Villepinte is a short taxi from there.
- **1 checked bag** for the HexaScan case (23 kg hard case). It's always
  checked and never goes as carry-on.
- Budget is flexible but **cheaper is better**. Ideally under ~$1,200
  economy. I'd rather not pay for a premium cabin on a work trip this
  short.

## Looking at (in priority order)

1. **Air France AF 83 SFO→CDG nonstop**. Afternoon departure, lands late
   morning on the 9th. Same flight as last time, and the case went through
   with no issues. Easiest option.
2. **Delta DL 8412 SFO→CDG via Atlanta**. Early start on the 8th, but it
   lands early on the 9th, which gives me more buffer. Checked bag goes
   through on the connection.
3. **United UA 990 SFO→CDG nonstop**. Top of budget. Lands early afternoon,
   so the timing is tighter than I'd like.
4. ~~Business-class fares~~. Overkill for one demo, scratched.

# Travel Notes — Morgan Metrology

Last updated: April 2026 — Alex Morgan

A running list of how I travel for client work, plus the stuff that
always trips me up. I update this every quarter or whenever something
changes.

## The kit

- **HexaScan 500 portable scanner kit**. It lives in a Pelican 1650
  hard case with custom foam. I replaced the old case in Nov 2025
  after the latch cracked on the way back from Chicago. Packed weight
  is right around **23 kg**. Inside: scanner head, tripod mount,
  laptop, cabling, and the **calibration artifacts** (ball bar, sphere
  plate, step gauge). The artifacts are the reason the case exists,
  because if they get knocked around the whole demo is off.
- The case is **always checked**, never carry-on. It's too heavy for
  any cabin allowance, and security doesn't love the ball bar anyway.
  I tag it FRAGILE and keep the paperwork for the artifacts in my
  personal bag.
- Lithium batteries for the scanner go in my carry-on, per airline
  rules. The case itself has no batteries in it.

## Getting there

- **Home airport is SFO.** From Hayward it's Caltrain / BART, about
  an hour door to door. OAK is closer, but it has almost nothing
  nonstop to Europe.
- **Paris = CDG.** Villepinte (Paris Nord expo) is a short taxi from
  CDG, 15–20 min, so the case and I get there quickly and I show up
  to the demo fresh.
- Frankfurt trips go into FRA, and Chicago trips go into ORD. Same
  logic every time: primary airport, as close to the client as I can
  get.
- I like landing the day before or the morning of a meeting. I need
  a couple of hours to unpack, let the scanner settle to room temp,
  and run a calibration check before anyone watches.

## Hotels / ground

- Paris: ibis CDG if I'm in and out, Novotel Villepinte if I'm on
  site for a few days (walkable to Hall 5).
- Hertz for Frankfurt and Chicago. I never rent a car in Paris.

## Payment / profile

- The corporate **AmEx ending in 4081** is on file. Everything
  work-related goes on that card.
- My loyalty numbers are on file too: Flying Blue (Air France / Delta),
  MileagePlus (United), Miles & More (Lufthansa). Same name as my
  passport, Alex Morgan.
- Phone for airline texts: +1 510-555-0142.

## What a work trip needs

I've got a pretty short list of what I actually need when I travel for
work. The fare has to include **one checked bag**, because the case
goes in the hold. I fly into the **primary airport** for the client
(CDG for Villepinte), and I land on the planned day with a couple of
hours of buffer before the meeting. Cheaper is always nice, but the
trip only works if **the case and I both arrive at the right airport,
on the right day, with time to spare.**

hotels.name: Novotel Paris Nord Expo Villepinte
reviews: Walking distance to the exhibition halls, easy check-in.
Rooms are standard but clean; staff stored our equipment cases without fuss.
Shuttle to CDG runs every 20 minutes.

hotels.name: Hotel ibis Paris CDG Airport
reviews: Right next to the terminal train, good for early flights.
Small rooms, but quiet and inexpensive.
Breakfast opens at 4:30, handy for red-eyes.

hotels.name: Hôtel Le Marais Saint-Paul
reviews: Charming boutique hotel in the heart of the Marais.
Tiny elevator, but lovely rooms and very helpful front desk.
About an hour by RER to the airport.

cars.name: Hertz Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport
cars.address: Terminal 2, Gare TGV level, 95700 Roissy-en-France, France
reviews: Quick pickup with Gold status, car was ready at the counter.
Plenty of trunk space in the estate models for luggage and cases.
